text: When a 4-DSP folded FIR on iCE40 misses 48 MHz at 44.6 MHz with a 33-cell LUT4 core.out_data path (11.67 ns logic + 9.35 ns route), switching to symmetry, fold=2, pipe_mul=1, and reg_in only reaches 45.0 MHz while doubling LUTs to 702, so pipeline the output lane-sum/accumulator stage directly instead of changing fold/symmetry, because the limiter is arithmetic depth in that LUT tree.

When an iCE40 folded symmetric FIR misses 48 MHz with a 32-bit accumulator and unregistered DSP output, set acc_width to 30 and enable the DSP output register to cut the core.out_data LUT4 stage from 33 to 28 cells, raising Fmax from 45.0 to 48.2 MHz (+3.2 MHz) and dropping 28 LUTs at unchanged 4 DSPs by shortening the accumulator carry chain and adding a pipe stage.

When an iCE40 symmetric folded FIR is timing-limited on a 28-cell core.out_data LUT4 path at 48.2 MHz with 4 DSPs and 674 LUTs, deepen folding from 2 to 4, widen the accumulator from 30 to 32 bits, and drop the DSP output register to cut DSPs to 2 and LUTs to 487 while raising Fmax to 50.5 MHz by shortening the per-cycle arithmetic depth and shifting the critical path to a shorter core.acc[1] stage.

For an iCE40 folded symmetric FIR already at max_dsp=4 and ~50 MHz, don't add a second post-multiplier fabric register (pipe_mul 1→2, dsp_regs out) while folding 4→2 and narrowing acc 32→29: it lost 0.9 MHz (50.45→49.52), added 173 LUT and 2 DSP, because the critical path shifted to the 30-LUT4 core.out_data sum/carry tree (11.19 ns logic + 7.61 ns route), so the bottleneck is the accumulator carry chain, not DSP-output isolation.

On an ice40 folded symmetric FIR at ~49.5 MHz with a 29-bit accumulator carry chain dominating the out_data path, keep the fabric DSP-output register: removing it lengthened that path's route delay from 7.61 ns to 8.8 ns and dropped Fmax to 47.4 MHz (-2.1 MHz), losing feasibility.

When an iCE40 folded symmetric FIR at fold=2 is timing-limited by the 29-bit accumulator carry chain from the registered SB_MAC16 output to out_data (11.2 ns LUT/carry + 7.6 ns route over ~30 cells), do not add a third multiplier-output pipeline stage (pipe_mul 2→3), because it only moved fmax 47.44→47.98 MHz at the same 660 LUT/4 DSP while the critical path still ran through the accumulator.

When an ice40 folded symmetric FIR at 47.98 MHz is timing-limited by the 29-bit accumulator carry chain from the registered multiplier output to core.out_data (11.19 ns LUT/carry plus 8.26 ns route), adding multiplier-side pipeline registers (pipe_mul=3,1 and dsp_regs=out+in_pipe_out) yields 0 MHz/LUT/DSP change, so leave multiplier registers alone and retime or shorten only the accumulator path.

When an iCE40 folded symmetric FIR is limited by the 29-bit accumulator carry chain (9.05 ns logic + 5.18 ns route) from the registered multiplier output to the part DFF, removing the input register (reg_in=false) raises Fmax by ~1.3 MHz (53.7→55.0 MHz) with one fewer LUT and unchanged DSP count, because the critical path starts at the registered multiplier output and the input FF only adds routing congestion.

When an iCE40 folded symmetric FIR is already DSP-count-capped at 4 DSPs and timing-limited by the min-width 29-bit accumulator carry chain (9.05 ns over 29 LUT4 plus 4.74 ns route), don't set reg_in=1 with dsp_regs=in_out: it only perturbs routing and leaves Fmax at 54.73 MHz versus 55.01 MHz while adding 1 LUT, because the carry-chain depth, not multiplier-output register placement, sets the critical path.

For an iCE40 folded symmetric FIR whose Fmax is set by the 29-bit accumulator carry chain at the legal minimum acc_width=29, do not drop a post-multiplier fabric pipeline stage ([2,1] on pipe_mul/dsp_regs in_out,out), because it lowered Fmax by 1.3 MHz (54.7 to 53.4 MHz) with unchanged 664 LUT/4 DSP since the carry chain still dominates (9.05 ns logic + 4.63 ns route across 29 LUT4 cells).

When an iCE40 folded symmetric FIR misses timing at 49.5 MHz on a 20.19 ns registered-multiplier-to-LUT path through the M=4 partial-sum/accumulator reduction (30 LUT4 cells, 11.19 ns logic + 7.61 ns route), enable the balanced registered sum_tree for that reduction, because it adds only 4 LUTs and 0 DSPs, shortens the arc to 18.62 ns, and lifts Fmax to 53.7 MHz by registering and balancing the M-way adder.

When an iCE40 folded symmetric FIR is timing-limited by the post-multiplier accumulator LUT4 reduction (29 cells, 9.05 ns logic + ~5 ns route) and the multiplier outputs are already registered, remove the input register (reg_in=false) instead of pipelining the multiplier side, because it cuts accumulator routing from 5.18 to 4.74 ns and raises Fmax by 1.3 MHz (53.7→55.0 MHz) at −1 LUT and no extra DSP.

On an iCE40 folded symmetric FIR whose fold=2 design is resource-heavy (663 LUT, 4 DSP) yet timing-limited by the DFF→29-LUT4 accumulator reduction, move to fold=4 with acc_width 30 and registered input to halve DSPs to 2 and cut LUTs to 475, but expect Fmax to stay flat or slightly drop (55.0→54.2 MHz) because the critical DFF→30-LUT4→DFF accumulator path (≈9.3 ns logic + 4.7 ns route) is not shortened.
